title: Evidence Collector Workbench for Enterprise Security Asks
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background:
Many enterprise sales and renewals stall on evidence requests: SOC2 attachments, DPA clauses, GDPR data flow diagrams, and bespoke vendor questionnaires. Currently, each ask generates an ad-hoc collection effort from Security, Legal, and Solutions Engineering which is slow and error-prone.

Goal:
Ship an internal Evidence Collector Workbench (ECW) MVP that reduces time-to-evidence for common enterprise asks by 60%, standardizes artifact packaging, and surfaces gaps to Sales/CS without excessive Security involvement. The tool should produce a signed evidence bundle (PDF + manifest) and an audit trail suitable for customer attachments and automated intake to Zendesk/GDrive.

Success metrics (first 90 days):
- Median time from request -> evidence bundle <= 48 hours for Tier 1 asks
- % of routine vendor questionnaire items auto-resolved >= 45%
- Reduction in Security manual hours on evidence collection by 40%
- Pilot with 3 strategic customers and CS team adoption rate >= 75%

Scope (MVP):
- Predefined templates for SOC2 artifact sets, DPA standard annexes, and GDPR data flow checklist
- Guided workflow for Solutions Engineers to select customer scope, attach artifacts, and flag proprietary gaps
- Enforcement of evidence hygiene (signed PDFs, versioned manifests, redaction hints)
- Export bundle with manifest and recommended cover letter templates
- Integration points: Confluence (artifact store), GitHub (link to control owners), Zendesk (ticket update), GDrive export

Out of scope (MVP):
- Full vendor questionnaire auto-fill using LLMs (prototype only)
- Legal approval automation (blocking; manual sign-off remains)

Proposed implementation approach:
- Product: define canonical artifact templates and mapping (PM + Security workshop)
- Design: low-friction stepper UI for Solutions Engineers + preview of final bundle
- Engineering: small backend service to assemble bundles, sign manifests, attach metadata, and push to Zendesk/GDrive; reuse existing RBAC and KMS integrations from Private onboarding code paths
- Security/Legal: review templates and approve redaction guidance; define sign-off gates for high-sensitivity items

Acceptance criteria:
1) ECW can produce a complete SOC2 evidence bundle from a checklist in <= 20 clicks
2) Bundle contains signed manifest, artifact fingerprints, and owner links to GitHub/Confluence
3) Export to Zendesk creates an update with bundle link and standardized subject line
4) UI shows clear next steps when evidence is missing (owner, suggested artifacts)
5) Security sign-off workflow is linked and tracked (manual)

Risks and trade-offs:
- Building too many templates up-front will delay delivery; mitigate with an iterative template backlog and an authoring UI for Security to add templates without eng changes.
- Automation of questionnaire answers has quality risk; prototype LLM-assist as separate spike and gate with manual review.
- Storing evidence centrally increases blast radius; ensure KMS encryption and audit logs.

Stakeholders:
- PM: Maya Chen (owner)
- Eng: Luca Martínez (lead), Priya Shah (backend), Aaron Li (frontend)
- Security: Dana O'Rourke (review), Rohit Patel (artifact mapping)
- Legal: Claire Dumont (sign-off)
- CS/Sales: Priya Kapoor (pilot partner)

Rollout plan:
- Week 1–2: Define templates + security review (workshop output committed)
- Week 3–4: Engineering sprint 1 (backend bundle service + Confluence/GDrive integration)
- Week 5–6: Frontend stepper + UX polish + internal alpha with Solutions Eng
- Week 7: Pilot with two strategic accounts; collect CS feedback and iterate
- Week 8: Expand pilot, freeze MVP, produce runbook and training docs

Artifacts and links:
- PRD (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood/company/ecw-prd (internal)
- Draft UI mockups (Figma): https://figma.com/file/abcdef/ECW-mockups (internal)
- Prototype LLM-assist spike repo: https://github.com/redwood/ecw-llm-prototype/pull/12
- Security template mapping spreadsheet: https://drive.redwood/reports/ecw-template-map.xlsx
- Zendesk macro example: https://zendesk.redwood/ticket/ECW-MACRO-EXAMPLE

Open questions:
- Which artifact retention period should be default (Security suggests 7 years for SOC2 artifacts)?
- Do we allow Solutions Eng to redact and re-upload artifacts before Legal sees them?
- Should the manifest include tokenized references to model outputs if we prototype LLM-assist?

Notes on compliance posture:
- KMS encryption must be applied to exported bundles. Engineering to leverage existing KMS/HSM integration paths from Private deployments.
- Presence of PII in evidence must trigger a tagging flow and manual Legal review.
